title: rubus micans subsp. pauciglandulosus
intro: Rubus micans subsp. pauciglandulosus, commonly known as the black thimbleberry, is a subspecies of the black raspberry plant that is native to North America. Research has shown that this plant has various health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can help protect against cell damage, reduce inflammation, and prevent infections. The therapeutic actions of Rubus micans subsp. pauciglandulosus include its ability to act as an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antiseptic, making it useful in treating wounds, reducing pain, and preventing infection. The bioactive constituents of this plant include anthocyanins, ellagic acid, and other phenolic compounds that are responsible for its therapeutic properties.
